description: Model of the Atari Punk Console, two 555 timers where the second stretches the pulses of the first and skips its cycles as it is stretched, with the capacitor charge curves brought out as saw waves

params.text: Sets the timing of the first timer, and with it the base frequency of the oscillator
Sets the timing of the second timer: from the left it widens the pulse, and past the point where the second timer runs longer than one cycle of the first it skips cycles, dropping the pitch in steps
Added to the TUNE and PW/SKIP settings at once, which sweeps the whole circuit while keeping the relationship between the two timers
Morphs between the three generated signals in a circle: SAW1 fully counter-clockwise, SAW2 a third of the way round, PULSE two thirds, then back to SAW1
Attenuates and inverts the TUNE input before it is added to the TUNE knob
Attenuates and inverts the PW/SKIP input before it is added to the PW/SKIP knob
Attenuates and inverts the BOTH input before it is added to the BOTH knob
Attenuates and inverts the WAVE input before it is added to the WAVE knob, despite the maker's tooltip naming it Wave, like the knob

inputs.text: A control voltage added to the TUNE setting, scaled by the TUNE attenuverter
A control voltage added to the PW/SKIP setting, scaled by the PW/SKIP attenuverter, which is what produces the abrupt octave jumps
A control voltage added to the BOTH setting, scaled by the BOTH attenuverter, which gives the widest range of usable sounds
A control voltage added to the WAVE setting, scaled by the WAVE attenuverter

outputs.text: The charge curve of the first timer's capacitor, a saw wave at the base frequency, with DC blocked
The square output of the second timer, which is the output of the original circuit, with DC blocked
The charge curve of the second timer's capacitor, which follows the skipping and so often runs lower in frequency than SAW1, with DC blocked
The three generated signals blended by the WAVE knob, with DC blocked

notes: there is no V/OCT input: this is not a precision oscillator and does not track pitch, so it is tuned by ear
